content.text:
The pattern is best explained by Ca2FeWO6 (mp-1276937) alone. I simulated three candidates (Ca2FeWO6, NaNdTi2O6 and Na2ZrWO6) and compared them to the observed peaks. I did not simulate the other six.

- **Ca2FeWO6 fits the peak shapes.** The observed peaks are near 19.6°, a doublet at 22.5/22.85°, a peak at about 32.3° with a shoulder near 31.95°, a doublet at 37.9/38.3°, and peaks around 46–48°, 58° and 68°. The simulated pattern has the same features at nearly the same positions, including the shoulder and both doublets.
- **The intensities don't match exactly.** Observed, the 19.6° peak is almost as strong as the main peak (about 97 against 100), but the simulation gives about 63. The higher-angle half of the 22–23° doublet is also stronger than simulated. A second candidate might explain this, but none of the ones I checked does.
- **NaNdTi2O6 doesn't fit.** Its simulated pattern has only a weak peak (about 4) near 22–23°, where the observed doublet reaches about 79. It also has a single peak near 38.7° instead of the observed doublet.
- **Na2ZrWO6 doesn't fit.** Its simulated strong peaks fall near 19.0°, 22.0° and 31.3°, where the observed pattern has nothing.
